sentiment.rationale: The company reported a comparable sales decline of 0.4% and acknowledged a slowdown in consumer spending, with management noting that the trend has continued into April. While the company reaffirmed its full-year guidance for low single-digit comp growth, it did not raise guidance and explicitly cited headwinds such as weather, consumer uncertainty, and tariffs. The cautious tone and lack of a positive forward revision, despite a modest EPS beat, lead to a negative sentiment score.

summary.revenue: Total revenue increased 6.4% to $2.9 billion for Q1 2025, driven by new restaurant openings.
summary.eps: Diluted EPS was $0.28, a 7.7% increase from $0.26; adjusted diluted EPS was $0.29, a 7.4% increase from $0.27.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 comparable restaurant sales growth expected in the low single digit range; 315-345 new company-owned restaurant openings; underlying effective tax rate between 25% and 27%.
summary.margin: Operating margin was 16.7%, up from 16.3%; restaurant level operating margin was 26.2%, down from 27.5%.
key_risks: Slowdown in consumer spending and economic uncertainty impacting transactions
Tariffs impacting cost of sales (estimated 50 basis points ongoing, 20 basis points in Q2) and new store builds (mid-single-digit increase)
Wage inflation, including minimum wage increases in California
Food cost inflation (avocados, dairy, chicken) and protein mix shift
Tough comparisons in Q2 (lapping 11.2% comp from last year)
Easter timing shift causing a 100 basis point headwind in Q2
key_opportunities: Chipotle Honey Chicken LTO driving incremental transactions and higher mix than prior LTOs
Back-of-house innovation (produce slicer, equipment package) expected to improve throughput and margins
Expansion plans: 315-345 new openings, international growth (Canada, Middle East, Mexico)
Strong value proposition with average entree under $10, 20-30% below comparable fast-casual meals
Digital and marketing initiatives to drive engagement and frequency
